skills.trigger: When evaluating a cystic or cavitary lung lesion on chest X-ray to distinguish between infectious, neoplastic, and congenital etiologies.
steps: Assess the wall thickness of the cavity or cyst; identify if it is thin-walled (suggesting congenital malformation or simple cyst) versus thick-walled (suggesting abscess, necrotizing pneumonia, or malignancy).
Check for the presence of an air-fluid level within the cavity, which indicates communication with the bronchial tree and superimposed infection or fluid accumulation.

Determine the precise anatomical location, specifically noting if the lesion is in the lower lobes (particularly the left lower lobe/retrocardiac region), as this distribution strongly favors intralobar pulmonary sequestration over upper-lobe predominant diseases like tuberculosis or emphysematous bullae.
